slides.slide_title: Intro to Autonomy of Cars and GPU Units

key_points: Transition from specialized 3D rendering units to general-purpose parallel processors.
Optimized for massive parallel processing, enabling efficient data-intensive tasks.
Core architecture supports high-performance computing, scientific simulations, and AI applications.

slides.slide_title: GPU's Role in AI and Deep Learning
key_points: Accelerates time-to-discovery in complex computational science.
Essential for training large neural networks, particularly in deep learning.
High core density and memory bandwidth support rapid model iteration and optimization.
Promises reduced traffic congestion and optimized fuel efficiency.
Aims to significantly lower accident rates caused by human error.
Challenges include technical, legal, and ethical hurdles in achieving Level 5 autonomy.

slides.slide_title: Sensor Fusion and Perception in AVs
key_points: Relies on advanced sensors like LiDAR, radar, and high-resolution cameras.
Accurate environmental perception is critical for safe navigation.
Integration of sensor data is essential for real-time decision-making.

slides.slide_title: GPU Architecture and Its Impact on AV Technology
key_points: Specialized hardware like Tensor Cores enhances deep learning capabilities.
Parallel architecture allows for processing of multiple data streams simultaneously.
Critical for real-time processing requirements in autonomous driving systems.

slides.slide_title: Business Value of Autonomous Vehicles and GPUs
key_points: Potential for significant cost savings through improved efficiency and safety.
Market growth driven by advancements in AI and GPU technology.
Investment in AV technology can lead to competitive advantages in transportation and logistics.
Continued evolution of GPU capabilities will enhance AV performance.
Ethical and regulatory frameworks will shape the deployment of autonomous vehicles.
Collaboration between tech and automotive industries is essential for innovation.
